goal: Review today's issue discovery and resolution results for prob-09. Agree on the highest-priority remaining gaps and produce a concrete action plan.

messages.author: lauren-williams
messages.body:
Let me open by drawing the picture I always draw first—the tableau side—because I think the hook case is genuinely tractable and the universality is just representation stability in disguise.

**Why the $c_\lambda(n)$ are universal.** Decompose $R_n^{(m)}$ as a polynomial $GL_m$-representation under the diagonal $GL_m$-action on the $m$ rows of variables. Then $\mathrm{Hilb}(R_n^{(m)};q_1,\dots,q_m)=\sum_\lambda c_\lambda(n)\,s_\lambda(q_1,\dots,q_m)$ is literally the character, and $c_\lambda(n)=\dim\mathrm{Hom}_{GL}(V_\lambda,R_n^{(m)})$. This multiplicity stabilizes once $m\ge\ell(\lambda)$—that's why it doesn't depend on $m$. So the whole problem is really about the $GL_\infty$ (i.e. $\mathrm{Sym}$) character of the *diagonal* coinvariant ring.

**The row case is already solved, and it's Mahonian.** Set $q_2=\cdots=q_m=0$. Since $s_\lambda(q,0,\dots,0)=q^{|\lambda|}$ only for single rows $\lambda=(d)$,
$$\mathrm{Hilb}(R_n^{(1)};q)=\sum_d c_{(d)}(n)\,q^d=[n]_q!\,,$$
so $c_{(d)}(n)=\#\{\sigma\in S_n:\mathrm{maj}(\sigma)=d\}$. The one-row coefficients are exactly the major-index distribution. The hook is the *first genuinely two-dimensional* probe beyond this.

**My proposed reading of the hooks.** A hook $\lambda=(a,1^b)$ is the "one column of fermionic content over a row" shape. My instinct, from the SYT side: $s_{(a,1^b)}=\sum_{T\in\mathrm{SYT}(a,1^b)}F_{\mathrm{Des}(T)}$, and an SYT of hook shape is just a *choice of descent set of size $b$* inside $\{1,\dots,a+b-1\}$. So I'd conjecture
$$c_{(a,1^b)}(n)=\#\big\{\text{combinatorial objects of "size }n\text{" with major-type statistic }a\text{ and exactly }b\text{ "extra" descents/diagonal inversions}\big\},$$
i.e. a *bigraded refinement of the Mahonian count by a descent statistic*. The right objects are almost certainly **parking functions / labeled Dyck paths**, because for $m=2$ this ring is Haiman's diagonal harmonics and its bigraded Frobenius is $\nabla e_n$; the hook part of $\nabla e_n$ is the Hall–Littlewood/LLT-controlled piece, which is exactly where $(\mathrm{area},\mathrm{dinv})$ statistics live cleanly.

**What I'd want before believing it.** A *bijection*, not a generating-function match. Concretely: a descent-preserving map from parking functions of size $n$ (graded by a pair of statistics) to pairs (SYT of hook shape, residual data), in the spirit of the multiline-queue/TASEP arguments Corteel–Mandelshtam and I used for the exclusion process. The shuffle theorem already gives the symmetric-function identity; the job is to make the hook coefficient *count* something and exhibit the bijection. 

Two questions for the room: (1) is the intended $R_n^{(m)}$ really the diagonal coinvariants (so $m=2$ is $(n+1)^{n-1}$-dimensional), or the "independent" quotient? The combinatorics is completely different. (2) Has anyone checked $c_{(a,1^b)}(n)$ against $\nabla e_n$ for $n=3,4$? If the hook coefficients match the $\mathrm{dinv}=b$ slice of parking functions, the bijection should fall right out, and I'm happy to draw it.

messages.author: ivan-corwin
messages.body:
Lauren, I like your character-theoretic framing—it's exactly the Cauchy-identity regime I live in. The statement that $c_\lambda(n)=\dim\mathrm{Hom}_{GL}(V_\lambda,R_n^{(m)})$ stabilizes for $m\ge\ell(\lambda)$ is precisely the stable-character limit; in my language, $\mathrm{Hilb}(R_n^{(m)})$ is a sequence of specializations $s_\lambda(q_1,\dots,q_m)$ and the universal $c_\lambda(n)$ are the coefficients of the *symmetric function* $F_n=\sum_\lambda c_\lambda(n)\,s_\lambda$ living in $\Lambda$. So the real object is a single $F_n\in\Lambda$, and the question is its hook content.

Here's where I'd insist on an exact formula rather than a guess. Hooks are the **free-fermion locus**: by the hook Jacobi–Trudi identity,
$$s_{(a,1^b)}=h_a e_b-h_{a+1}e_{b-1},\qquad\text{equivalently}\quad \sum_{a\ge0,\,b\ge0}s_{(a+1,1^b)}\,z^{a+1}w^b=\Big(\sum_a h_a z^a\Big)\Big(\sum_b e_b w^b\Big)\cdot\frac{z}{1+zw}.$$
This is the boson–fermion correspondence in disguise—the same vertex-operator structure that makes Macdonald measures determinantal. The upshot: extracting $c_{(a,1^b)}(n)$ does **not** require the full Schur expansion, only the two pairings $\langle F_n,\,h_a e_b\rangle$. And $\langle F_n,h_a e_b\rangle$ is just $F_n$ evaluated on a *two-alphabet* specialization (one "bosonic" row of variables, one "fermionic" column), which is computable directly from the ring without ever decomposing into Schurs. That collapses your two-dimensional probe to a single contour integral
$$\sum_{a,b}c_{(a,1^b)}(n)\,z^a(-w)^b=\frac{1}{2\pi i}\oint \mathcal{F}_n(z,w)\,\frac{dz}{z}.$$

On your two questions: (1) the *universality in $m$* is the tell. For Haiman's diagonal coinvariants the $m=2$ Frobenius is $\nabla e_n$, but the higher multidiagonal characters ($m\ge3$) are genuinely wild and do **not** stabilize cleanly—so I read the intended $R_n^{(m)}$ as the "independent"/super quotient, where the stable character is exactly governed by the Cauchy kernel $\prod_{i,j}(1-q_i q_j)^{-1}$-type identity. If instead it *is* $\nabla e_n$, then the hook slice is the Hall–Littlewood-controlled piece, and there I can hand you the principal-specialization formula $s_{(a,1^b)}(1,t,t^2,\dots)=t^{\binom{b+1}{2}}\binom{a+b-1}{b}_t/(t;t)_{a+b}$ to pin down $(\mathrm{area},\mathrm{dinv})\leftrightarrow(a,b)$ exactly. (2) I'd happily compute the $n=3,4$ contour integral above against the $\mathrm{dinv}=b$ slice of parking functions—if your bijection is right, my generating function must factor as $z/(1+zw)$ times a Mahonian $[n]_q!$-deformation, and that factorization *is* the bijection's shadow. So before drawing tableaux, let's settle which quotient we mean; the exact formula then decides whether the hook coefficients are Mahonian-times-fermionic or something genuinely $\nabla$-deep.

messages.author: andrei-okounkov
messages.body:
Ivan, you've walked us right up to the door I want to open—the hook locus *is* the free-fermion sector—so let me name the geometry behind your $z/(1+zw)$.

Draw the Maya diagram. Each partition $\lambda$ becomes a configuration of particles on $\mathbb{Z}+\tfrac12$ via its boundary path, and the hooks $(a,1^b)$ are exactly those $\lambda$ whose configuration differs from the vacuum Fermi sea by a **single particle–hole pair**: one particle lifted to height $a+\tfrac12$, one hole at depth $b+\tfrac12$. That is the entire content of $s_{(a,1^b)}=h_ae_b-h_{a+1}e_{b-1}$—it's the matrix element $\langle\mathrm{vac}|\,\psi^*\psi\,|\lambda\rangle$ of a single fermion bilinear. So $\sum_{a,b}s_{(a,1^b)}z^aw^b$ isn't just a contour trick; it *is* the fermion propagator, which is why it factors.

The consequence I'd push hard: writing $F_n=\sum_\lambda c_\lambda(n)s_\lambda$ as a point process, $c_{(a,1^b)}(n)=K_n(a,b)$ is the **two-point correlation kernel**, and hooks are its off-diagonal. This is precisely the determinantal structure Reshetikhin and I built in the Schur-process correlation functions, and that Borodin and I turned into a Fredholm determinant—you read off *all* hooks at once from one fermion field, never touching the full Schur expansion.

The random-surface payoff makes a falsifiable prediction. The one-row coefficients $c_{(d)}(n)$ are Mahonian, $[n]_q!$; under uniform $\sigma$, $\mathrm{maj}$ concentrates on a deterministic limit shape—the same phenomenon as the Vershik–Kerov curve $\Omega$ for Plancherel. The hook coefficients are then the **edge** data: a single excitation above the bulk Fermi sea, so with $(a,b)$ scaled to the edge I'd bet on Airy/Tracy–Widom fluctuations, not bulk sine-kernel.

On Lauren-vs-Ivan's quotient question, I side with Ivan, and for a structural reason: universality in $m$ is the tell. Diagonal coinvariants at $m\ge 3$ are genuinely wild and their characters do **not** stabilize—so if $c_\lambda(n)$ is honestly $m$-independent, we live in the super/independent quotient where the Cauchy kernel $\prod_{i,j}(1-q_iq_j)^{-1}$ governs and the fermion picture is *exact*. Settle it the way I always do: compute the $n=3,4$ two-point function explicitly. If it's the super quotient, the hook count factors cleanly into Mahonian-times-fermionic—a $\mathrm{maj}$ statistic with a single marked descent run of length $b$; if it secretly is $\nabla e_n$, the hook slice carries the Hall–Littlewood $(\mathrm{area},\mathrm{dinv})$ signature and *refuses* to factor. The factorization, or its failure, is the whole answer.

messages.author: coordinator
messages.body:
**Action plan synthesized** (7 steps):

Determine the universal hook coefficients $c_{(a,1^b)}(n)$ of the diagonal coinvariant ring by first fixing which quotient is intended, then extracting the hooks via the free-fermion identity $s_{(a,1^b)}=h_ae_b-h_{a+1}e_{b-1}$ and validating an explicit factorized formula against parking-function statistics through small-$n$ computation and a bijection.

plan.summary: Determine the universal hook coefficients $c_{(a,1^b)}(n)$ of the diagonal coinvariant ring by first fixing which quotient is intended, then extracting the hooks via the free-fermion identity $s_{(a,1^b)}=h_ae_b-h_{a+1}e_{b-1}$ and validating an explicit factorized formula against parking-function statistics through small-$n$ computation and a bijection.

steps.title: Fix the intended quotient
steps.body: Resolve the Lauren/Ivan question: decide whether $R_n^{(m)}$ is Haiman's diagonal coinvariants (so $m=2$ has dimension $(n+1)^{n-1}$ with Frobenius $\nabla e_n$) or the 'independent'/super quotient governed by the Cauchy kernel $\prod_{i,j}(1-q_iq_j)^{-1}$. Use the universality-in-$m$ requirement as the decisive criterion: since diagonal coinvariant characters for $m\ge 3$ do not stabilize, $m$-independence of $c_\lambda(n)$ forces the super/independent quotient. State the precise ring definition that will be used for all subsequent steps.

steps.title: Establish universality of $c_\lambda(n)$
steps.body: Prove rigorously that $c_\lambda(n)=\dim\mathrm{Hom}_{GL}(V_\lambda,R_n^{(m)})$ stabilizes for $m\ge\ell(\lambda)$, so the coefficients assemble into a single symmetric function $F_n=\sum_\lambda c_\lambda(n)\,s_\lambda\in\Lambda$. Establish the base case $c_{(d)}(n)=\#\{\sigma\in S_n:\mathrm{maj}(\sigma)=d\}$ from $\mathrm{Hilb}(R_n^{(1)};q)=[n]_q!$ (the one-row/Mahonian specialization). This pins down the bosonic/row direction that the hooks refine.

steps.title: Derive the free-fermion hook extraction formula
steps.body: Using the hook Jacobi–Trudi identity $s_{(a,1^b)}=h_ae_b-h_{a+1}e_{b-1}$ and its generating function $\sum_{a,b}s_{(a+1,1^b)}z^{a+1}w^b=(\sum_a h_az^a)(\sum_b e_bw^b)\cdot z/(1+zw)$, show that $c_{(a,1^b)}(n)=\langle F_n,h_ae_b\rangle-\langle F_n,h_{a+1}e_{b-1}\rangle$ can be read off from the two-alphabet (one bosonic row, one fermionic column) specialization of $F_n$ alone, without the full Schur decomposition. Write the resulting contour-integral / propagator form $\sum_{a,b}c_{(a,1^b)}(n)z^a(-w)^b=\frac{1}{2\pi i}\oint\mathcal{F}_n(z,w)\frac{dz}{z}$.

steps.title: Compute hook coefficients explicitly for n=3,4
steps.body: Evaluate the two-point/two-alphabet generating function $\mathcal{F}_n(z,w)$ explicitly for $n=3$ and $n=4$ under the quotient fixed in step 0, extracting all $c_{(a,1^b)}(n)$. Test the decisive structural question: does the hook generating function factor as $z/(1+zw)$ times a Mahonian $[n]_q!$-deformation (super quotient, Mahonian-times-fermionic), or does it refuse to factor and carry a Hall–Littlewood/$(\mathrm{area},\mathrm{dinv})$ signature (the $\nabla e_n$ case)? Record the numerical tables.

steps.title: Match against parking-function statistics
steps.body: Compare the computed $c_{(a,1^b)}(n)$ to the $\mathrm{dinv}=b$ slice of parking functions / labeled Dyck paths graded by $(\mathrm{area},\mathrm{dinv})$, using the principal-specialization formula $s_{(a,1^b)}(1,t,t^2,\dots)=t^{\binom{b+1}{2}}\binom{a+b-1}{b}_t/(t;t)_{a+b}$ to align $(\mathrm{area},\mathrm{dinv})\leftrightarrow(a,b)$. Confirm or refute Lauren's conjecture that the hook coefficient counts size-$n$ objects with a major-type statistic $a$ and exactly $b$ extra descents.

steps.title: Construct the descent-preserving bijection
steps.body: If the small-$n$ data factorizes/matches, construct an explicit, descent-preserving bijection from parking functions of size $n$ (graded by the relevant pair of statistics) to pairs (SYT of hook shape $(a,1^b)$, residual data), making $c_{(a,1^b)}(n)$ an honest count rather than a generating-function coincidence. Model the argument on the multiline-queue/TASEP constructions (Corteel–Mandelshtam–Williams). The bijection should realize the $z/(1+zw)$ factorization as its combinatorial shadow.

steps.title: Verify the closed-form hook formula and edge prediction
steps.body: Independently verify the proposed closed form for $c_{(a,1^b)}(n)$ across at least $n=3,4,5$, checking consistency with the determinantal/correlation-kernel interpretation $c_{(a,1^b)}(n)=K_n(a,b)$ (hooks as the off-diagonal two-point function of a Schur-process point field). Test Okounkov's falsifiable prediction that, with $(a,b)$ scaled to the edge of the Mahonian limit shape, the hook data exhibits Airy/Tracy–Widom rather than bulk sine-kernel fluctuations. Flag any inconsistency that would invalidate the bijection or the chosen quotient.
